exclusions.reason: The analytic first-harmonic cosine coefficient is zero. Rumoca and OMC both leave integration residue, and Rumoca's residual is closer to zero; OMC's near-zero reference spread makes normalized pointwise comparison non-identifying.

The MSL model is explicitly chaotic and runs for 50000 seconds. Exponential trajectory separation makes one solver's pointwise trajectory non-identifying; this model requires invariant or statistical comparison.

At the 0.1 s input step, OMC records the pre-event PIA resistor loss powers at t=0.1 and the post-event values at t=0.1000000001100004, while Rumoca records the post-event values at t=0.1. The post-event peak agrees to floating-point precision and 281/283 channels are strict-high; the two minor channels are aliases of this event-side output convention, so raw pointwise interpolation is non-identifying.

At the 0.1 s current-command step, OMC records the pre-event PID error at t=0.1 and the post-event value at t=0.1000000001100014, while Rumoca records the post-event value at t=0.1. The seven minor channels are PID error aliases of this event-side phase shift; all 200 other channels are strict-high and the post-event response agrees, so raw pointwise interpolation at the discontinuity is non-identifying.

The differing channels are period Mean/RMS aggregates at integration-residue scale within the model's 1e-6 experiment tolerance; waveform channels agree and Rumoca's mean is closer to the analytic 3*sqrt(6)/pi*Vrms value.

Only aliases of the period-integrated RootMeanSquare/Mean aggregate differ. At the annotation tolerance of 1e-6, OMC's endpoint RMS is 109.999434852 V; rerunning the same generated OMC model at 1e-10 moves it to 110.000018546 V, a 5.84e-4 V shift that accounts for Rumoca's 5.74e-4 V difference. The physical waveform and state channels agree, so the default-tolerance OMC trace is not converged enough to identify pointwise aggregate parity.

Tiny PWM event-time shifts make raw pointwise comparison of the held aggregate non-identifying; the switching waveform and physical states agree, and both solvers converge to the same 19.999995992 V endpoint within 2.7e-10 V.
